skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

version.changelog:
**smyx-grooming-effectiveness-analysis 1.0.5**

- Updated internal utility scripts for improved maintainability.
- Removed redundant documentation file (`skill-card.md`).
- Minor documentation updates in SKILL.md.
- No changes to core analysis workflow or API behavior.

llm.summary: This skill appears to perform the advertised pet grooming media analysis, but it also creates or reuses account identity, stores tokens locally, and queries cloud history with limited user-facing consent.

dimensions.detail: Remote image/video analysis is coherent with the stated purpose, and history reports are documented, but the implementation also performs identity resolution, silent account registration/login, token handling, and local user persistence that materially broaden the capability surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly tells the agent not to ask users about internal identity values and automatically triggers cloud history queries; this is operationally scoped but under-discloses account-bound behavior to end users.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution or destructive setup was observed. A static warning points to a private raw-IP development endpoint in config-dev.yaml, but the packaged default config selects prod, so this is not the main concern.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code reads environment-provided OpenClaw identity/workspace context and a workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt file, then sends account identifiers and media or media URLs to remote service endpoints; this is only partly proportionate to the analysis purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The shared utility creates a workspace data SQLite database, creates/alters a sys_user table, persists generated users and returned tokens/openTokens, and has no clear retention or cleanup control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It sends provided pet images/videos or URLs to a remote service, may automatically create or reuse an internal account identity, can retrieve cloud-stored history, and stores user/token data in a local workspace database. Install only if that account-bound remote processing and local persistence are acceptable for your workspace.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic DAO filters are real generic database behavior, but they are not the primary user-facing path and do not by themselves show malicious execution or exfiltration.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill uses shell-invoked Python scripts, filesystem reads/writes, local database storage, and remote APIs without a separate permission declaration; SKILL.md describes some but not all of this behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: The --list cloud history feature is documented in SKILL.md and tied to historical trend reporting, but it increases privacy impact because it retrieves account-associated historical records.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Identity creation/reuse, phoneLogin/register, local token persistence, and broad shared CRUD/API helpers go beyond simple grooming-media analysis and are not clearly bounded to one narrow workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media analysis and local attachment handling are partly disclosed, but the account identity, token transmission, local credential-file reuse, and retention details are not clear enough for informed consent.
[E1] unexpected: The outbound phoneLogin/register request sends openId/mobile/source as a side effect of ordinary API use; this is account provisioning behavior, not just media analysis.
[suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The private-IP endpoint is present only in a development config file while the active packaged config is prod, so this finding is downgraded and is not the verdict driver.
